requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the most likely hazards you may encounter while participating in geocaching activities, and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, and respond to these hazards. (b) Discuss first aid and prevention for the types of injuries or illnesses that could occur while participating in geocaching activities, including cuts, scrapes, snakebite, insect stings, tick bites, exposure to poisonous plants, heat and cold reactions (sunburn, heatstroke, heat exhaustion, hypothermia), and dehydration. (c) Discuss how to properly plan an activity that uses GPS, including using the buddy system, sharing your plan with others, and considering the weather, route, and proper attire.

pamphlet_excerpts: Hazards, First Aid & Safety: Learn how to recognize, and avoid, the poisonous plants in your area, such as poison ivy, poison oak, and poison sumac (p. 66).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 2: If you think you have touched a poisonous plant, immediately wash the affected skin with soap and water (p. 66).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 3: Wipe with rubbing alcohol and apply a soothing skin treatment such as calamine lotion (p. 66).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 4: Prevent sunburn by limiting exposure to the sun, covering up, and wearing a broad-brimmed hat (p. 66).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Use a sunscreen with a sun protection factor (SPF) of at least 15 (p. 66).
Step 2 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Treat a painful sunburn by applying cool, wet cloths (p. 66).
Step 3 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Stay in the shade if possible, and cover up (long pants, long-sleeved shirt, a brimmed hat) to avoid further overexposure to the sun (p. 66).
Step 4 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Symptoms can include pale, clammy skin; nausea and headache; dizziness and fainting; muscle cramps; and weakness or lack of energy (p. 66).

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) If a Cache to Eagle® series exists in your council, visit at least three of the locations in the series. Release your Travel Bug into a public geocache and, with your parent or guardian's permission, monitor its progress at www. geocaching. com for 30 days. Keep a log, and share this with your counselor at the end of the 30-day period. (c) Set up and hide a public geocache, following the guidelines in the Geocaching merit badge pamphlet. Before doing so, share with your counselor a three-month maintenance plan for the geocache where you are personally responsible for those three months. After setting up the geocache, with your parent or guardian's permission, follow the logs online for 30 days and share them with your counselor. You must archive the geocache when you are no longer maintaining it. (d) Explain what Cache In Trash Out (CITO) means, and describe how you have practiced CITO at public geocaches or at a CITO event. Then, either create CITO containers to leave at public caches, or host a CITO event for your unit or for the public.
